main_text.head: CAELII S. C. IN M. T. CICERONIS PARTITIONES ORATORIAS EXPLICATIONUM LIBER PRIMUS.
INSCRIPTIONIS EXPLICATIO: id est, cur Partitiones appellatae, & de Methodo pauca.
main_text.p:
Artitiones appellauit Cicero, hunc de arte Rhetorica absolutissimum dialogum, propterea quòd artem ea methodo tradere propofuit, quæ διαίρεσις siue διαίρεσις appellatur: in qua sumpta artis definitione, à summis generibus ad ultimas usq; partes & formas progreditur: ex quibus demum tota ars constituitur. quæ ratio docendi cõmodissima est, & ad recordandum aptissima: idcirco à Platone ipso, itemq; Cicerone & Galeno usitata. Est autem Methodus, autore Galeno, uniuersalis quedam uia & ratio, omnium singularium eiusdem generis, qua omnia recte inueniuntur, & inuenta approbantur: quæ uero perperam habent, redarguuntur. Nam qui methodo utitur, uerba in primis, quibus utendum est, si obscura sint, explicat, atq; distinguit: res definit, definitas diuidit: à summis
b mis

page.notes: The woodcut initial "A" is decorative and joined to "rtitiones" as printed. Library stamp at right and show-through marks omitted. The Greek words in the second paragraph (διαίρεσις) are reproduced as best read; the first may be διαιρετικὴ. Line-end words "Artitiones" likely reads "Partitiones" with the initial P under the woodcut; left as read. Marginal mark "Alethas" at right edge is a printed or stamped mark and is uncertain.
